PullRequest.Title: chat: Attribute admin-enforced restrictions to "your organization"
PullRequest.Body:
Follow-up to #343302. Reviewers said "Disabled by policy" doesn't make clear who enforces the restriction. It's the user's organization or enterprise admins, not VS Code. This PR standardizes user-facing wording across the app. | State | Label | Hover / ARIA | |---|---|---| | Unavailable | **Disabled by your organization** | "…Contact your administrator." | | Set and locked | **Managed by your organization** | "…can't be changed." | | Forced on | **Required by your organization** | | "Your organization" covers both GitHub org-level and enterprise-level policies. It was already the most common wording (the Agent Host picker, GitHub Environments, MCP, plugins, the Settings editor). The `$(briefcase)` icon and "Learn why" links are unchanged. ### Changes - **Permissions picker** (Agent Host and Agents window): "Disabled by policy" becomes "Disabled by your organization". The hover and ARIA text say "Contact your administrator." - **Local harness:** "Disabled by policy · Learn why" and "Disabled by enterprise policy" become "Disabled by your organization". The hover reads "Your organization requires the Copilot harness." - **Settings editor:** "Managed by organization" becomes "Managed by your organization". - **Retired wording** ("organization policy", "your organization's policy", "via policy", "your organization admin", "your organization administrator"): - Agents overlay - Update tooltip - GitHub Environments - MCP and plugin views, managed-plugin retry, plugin install - MCP server and extension blocking - Session settings provider - Sandbox toggle - Accessibility help - Permission setting descriptions - Copilot extension (external ingest, session sync) - Unit tests and the policy smoke test now expect the new strings. ### Screenshots From the [screenshot diff report](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/344670#issuecomment-6457257646).

### Intentionally unchanged - Admin-facing policy descriptions, policy readiness reports, and context key descriptions. - llama.cpp `runtimeBlocked` ("Blocked by policy"). It fires on EPERM or code-signing failures, which may come from the OS rather than the organization. - Copilot runtime-provided messages used as test fixtures (e.g. "required by your organization admin" in `copilotAgentSession.test.ts`). ### Validation - **Not run:** compile, type check, and unit tests. `npm ci` failed in the authoring sandbox because `electronjs.org` couldn't be reached for native module headers (`@vscode/spdlog`). A local agent will run validation on this draft. - All changes are inside string literals. Quoting and escaping were reviewed in the diff, and a grep confirms no remaining references to the old strings in tests. ### How to test 1. Configure a policy that disables a permission level (e.g. `permissions.disableBypassPermissionsMode`). Open the Permissions picker: the option shows "$(briefcase) Disabled by your organization", and its hover mentions contacting your administrator. 2. Configure a policy that requires the Copilot harness. Open the harness picker: Local shows "Disabled by your organization · Learn why". 3. In the Settings editor, open a policy-managed setting: it shows "Managed by your organization". 4. Run the affected tests: ``` ./scripts/test.sh --grep "permission|Permission|sessionTarget|ModePicker|ManagedPluginRetry|mcpListWidget|SettingIndicators|settingsTree|SandboxToggle|toggleRemoteConnections|MainThreadMcp|Extension Management" ```

Scenarios.Scenario: Render policy-managed chat, session, MCP/plugin, settings, update, and permission-picker UI states
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Existing state evaluation and UI rendering must complete; the diff only substitutes localized default strings on the same render path.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of visible policy-managed controls or list rows; each existing render still performs one equivalent string lookup/assignment per affected element.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Unchanged synchronous UI rendering; no new queue, limiter, parallel work, or re-entrant scheduling.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Localization lookup keys and existing UI lifecycle are unchanged; no cache keys, misses, invalidation, coalescing, or negative-cache behavior changed.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence that only literal text changes: all production hunks preserve control flow and APIs, and matching test hunks only update expected text.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Longer labels can occupy slightly more visual space, but the diff provides no mechanism for extra layout passes or materially greater rendering work.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The diff neither adds synchronous work nor changes rendering frequency, cardinality, retention, or lifecycle.

Scenarios.Scenario: Display policy-blocked notifications, errors, status text, accessibility help, and filesystem-provider denial messages
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Existing error/status construction remains on the same critical path; only message contents differ.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Existing occurrences of policy-denied actions or status refreshes; the diff does not increase their count or fan-out.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Unchanged; no asynchronous operation, retry, process, IPC, filesystem, database, or network request is added or moved.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache or memoization behavior is touched; cold and warm behavior are identical apart from returned text.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence from all changed production hunks: object construction, notification dispatch, and error creation are unchanged.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The replacement strings differ by a few characters, with negligible bounded allocation differences and no unbounded payload.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. There is no new boundary, repeated work, serialization, or meaningful allocation scaling.

Scenarios.Scenario: Run updated unit and smoke assertions for organization-policy wording
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Test execution performs the same setup, rendering, and assertions with replacement expected strings.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Fixed existing test cases and DOM queries; assertion cardinality is unchanged.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Unchanged test-runner concurrency; no additional tests, waits, polling loops, or retries were introduced.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No production or test cache behavior changed.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence because test hunks solely replace expected text or substring literals.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: None material for performance review; literal comparison lengths change only by a bounded number of characters.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass across all 34 changed files and every diff page. The PR consistently replaces organization-policy wording in bounded localized strings and corresponding tests; it adds no expensive boundary, hot-path work, concurrency, retained state, cache change, or performance regression. No findings or regression-fix records were warranted.
